```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 09_power_calculation_practice
title: >
  Calculate power for a new study
questions:
  - id: new_design_power
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      For a two-tailed $z$ test with $\alpha = .05$, suppose $\mu_0 = 100$,
      $\sigma = 20$, and $n = 25$. What is the power to detect a true population
      mean of $\mu_1 = 108$? Assume normal sampling distributions with the same
      population SD under both hypotheses. Enter power as a proportion from 0
      to 1. You can use the [unit normal table](06-probability.qmd#tbl-unit-normal).
    hints:
      - >
        First calculate the standard error, $\sigma_M = \sigma/\sqrt{n}$.
      - >
        With a two-tailed $\alpha = .05$, the critical $z$ scores are about
        $\pm 1.96$. Convert them to raw sample means using
        $M = \mu_0 + z\sigma_M$.
      - >
        Locate those same critical means relative to the alternative mean of
        108. Find the area between their alternative-distribution $z$ scores
        to get $\beta$, then subtract it from 1.
      - >
        The lower boundary is nearly four standard errors below the alternative
        mean. Its left-tail area rounds to .0000, so it contributes very little
        to the calculation.
    answer: 0.516
    tolerance: 0.005
    min: 0
    max: 1
    explanation: |
      The standard error is $20/\sqrt{25} = 4$. The null critical means are
      $100 - 1.96(4) = 92.16$ and $100 + 1.96(4) = 107.84$.

      Relative to the alternative distribution, their $z$ scores are
      $(92.16 - 108)/4 = -3.96$ and $(107.84 - 108)/4 = -.04$.
      The area to the left of $-.04$ is about .4840; the area to the left of
      $-3.96$ rounds to .0000. So $\beta \approx .4840$, and
      power $\approx 1 - .4840 = .5160$.

      The design would detect this specified effect about 52 percent of the
      time over repeated studies. Power includes both rejection tails,
      although the far-left tail contributes very little here.
```
